title: The Vow of Port Alder
premise: Quentin Kavanagh, a wedding planner who swore off believing in love after her own engagement collapsed, takes one last job in the fading seaside town of Port Alder — planning the wedding of a stranger's cousin to survive a family reunion, with bakery owner Marisol Vega as her fake date. What begins as a convenient lie deepens as Quentin uncovers that Marisol's bakery lease is being quietly stolen by the same developer who ruined Quentin's career years ago. As the wedding approaches and the lease deadline looms, Quentin must choose between protecting herself and fighting for Marisol's found family of dockworkers, bakers, and strays — and for a love she stopped believing she deserved. In the end, the wedding becomes a public reckoning: the town exposes the developer's forged documents, Marisol keeps her bakery, and Quentin finally lets someone stay after the last train leaves.
about_author: Oscar Ishikawa is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent a decade watching other people's happiest days before writing about them instead. They live near a harbor, where they collect tide charts and insist every good love story needs a deadline.

chapters.title: The Last Contract
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She signs what she swears is her final wedding contract — a reunion-wedding in Port Alder — while packing up her failing planning business. Emotional beat: weary resignation masking grief over her broken engagement and ruined reputation.

chapters.title: Reunion Rules
chapters.summary: Quentin arrives at the Kavanagh family reunion dreading questions about her ex-fiancé. Her aunt announces a cousin's wedding will happen during the reunion week. Beat: claustrophobic family pressure.

chapters.title: A Date at the Bakery
chapters.summary: To deflect matchmaking, Quentin blurts that she's seeing someone. She ducks into the nearest shop — Marisol Vega's bakery — and begs a stranger to play along. Beat: panicked improvisation turning into unexpected chemistry.

chapters.title: Flour and Falsehoods
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She agrees to the fake date for reasons she doesn't examine too closely, charmed despite herself by Quentin's honesty about the lie. Beat: reluctant amusement, first spark.

chapters.title: Dessert Was the Problem
chapters.summary: The fake date at the reunion dinner goes too well; their story feels seamless, their laughter unforced. Quentin's mother is delighted. Beat: the moment pretending stops feeling like pretending.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Quentin proposes they keep the ruse going through the wedding — it helps her professionally and shields Marisol from her own meddling relatives. Marisol hesitates, then agrees. Beat: a bargain both know is dangerous.

chapters.title: The Lease on Larkspur Lane
chapters.summary: Marisol mentions her bakery lease expires the same week as the wedding, and the landlord, developer Corliss Hume, is pressuring her to sell. Quentin recognizes the name. Beat: quiet dread.

chapters.title: The Man Who Took Everything
chapters.summary: Flashback woven into present: Hume's forged contracts destroyed Quentin's old firm and her engagement five years ago. She never proved it. Beat: old wound reopened, resolve kindling.

chapters.title: Sunday Regulars
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. We meet her found family: retired dockworker Edda, runaway teen Theo who sleeps in the storeroom, and widower Father Bram. Beat: warmth, showing what Quentin stands to lose if the bakery falls.

chapters.title: Site Visit
chapters.summary: Quentin scouts wedding venues and notices Hume's surveyors measuring the bakery block. She photographs them on instinct. Beat: suspicion hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Practice Makes Pretend
chapters.summary: Rehearsing couple stories over wine, Quentin and Marisol accidentally tell each other true things. First almost-kiss, interrupted by Theo. Beat: ache of wanting more than the arrangement allows.

chapters.title: The Cousin's Chaos
chapters.summary: Wedding-planning chapter: the bride, Priya, is overwhelmed and her fiancé is distant. Quentin, jaded, finds herself caring again. Beat: professional cynicism cracking.

chapters.title: Edda's Ledger
chapters.summary: Edda reveals half the waterfront tenants got identical 'voluntary buyout' letters with impossible deadlines. Quentin recognizes Hume's signature clause style. Beat: pattern recognition, shared anger.

chapters.title: Last Train Out
chapters.summary: After a festival night, Marisol misses the last train home; Quentin offers her couch. A tender, guarded conversation about why neither believes in second chances. Beat: intimacy without permission.

chapters.title: Hume at the Door
chapters.summary: Corliss Hume visits the bakery personally, all charm and veiled threats, and recognizes Quentin. He implies he remembers her 'little meltdown' years ago. Beat: fear weaponized against her.

chapters.title: What Quentin Buried
chapters.summary: Quentin confesses everything to Marisol: the forged contract, the fiancé who believed the worst, the career collapse. Marisol believes her instantly. Beat: vulnerability met with faith — the turn.

chapters.title: Theo Runs
chapters.summary: Theo's estranged father shows up with Hume's money behind him, threatening custody unless the boy leaves town. Marisol's family closes ranks. Beat: stakes become personal and urgent.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Quentin pulls county records and finds discrepancies in the original 1998 deed Hume cites — signatures that don't match. Beat: hope with sharp edges; justice may be provable.

chapters.title: Priya's Doubt
chapters.summary: The bride nearly cancels the wedding after finding her fiancé's secret debts. Quentin talks her through it, surprising herself with sincerity. Beat: the non-believer defending marriage.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Alone after a successful tasting, Quentin and Marisol kiss — then Marisol pulls back, terrified of losing the bakery and the friendship if this fails. Beat: longing colliding with self-protection.

chapters.title: Cold Storage
chapters.summary: Awkward professionalism follows. Quentin throws herself into discovering Hume bought the county clerk's silence. Beat: heartbreak converted into investigation.

chapters.title: Father Bram's Confession
chapters.summary: Bram admits he witnessed the original deed signing decades ago and was paid to forget details. His guilt gives Quentin a witness. Beat: redemption offered to a minor character, courage contagious.

chapters.title: Deadline Math
chapters.summary: Lease expires three days after the wedding. Hume files an eviction notice early, citing a technicality. Beat: the clock starts ticking audibly.

chapters.title: The Town Meeting
chapters.summary: Quentin organizes tenants to share documents publicly. Hume's lawyer intimidates the room; only Edda stands and speaks. Beat: fear versus solidarity, solidarity winning narrowly.

chapters.title: Marisol's Reason
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She reveals the bakery was her late mother's dream and why she can't leave Port Alder — and admits she pulled away because Quentin has one foot out of town. Beat: honest collision of fears.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal Dinner Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone leaks that Quentin's fake relationship is a ruse, humiliating her before her whole family. Hume's fingerprints are on the leak. Beat: public shame, private fury.

chapters.title: Standing in the Wreckage
chapters.summary: Instead of denying it, Quentin tells her family the truth — including why she stopped believing in weddings. Her mother, unexpectedly, apologizes for years of pressure. Beat: liberation through honesty.

chapters.title: Marisol Chooses
chapters.summary: Marisol publicly takes Quentin's hand at the bakery, ending the pretense on her own terms. The town watches. Beat: defiant tenderness.

chapters.title: Hume's Counterstrike
chapters.summary: Hume gets the wedding venue condemned with a bogus safety order, hoping to break Quentin's last contract and credibility together. Beat: antagonist at full strength, lowest point approaching.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: With two days left, the team scatters: Theo hacks public filing databases, Edda rallies dockworkers, Bram agrees to testify. Beat: scrappy momentum, found family as machinery of justice.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Theo finds the original deed's second page misfiled under a defunct company — proving Hume's chain of title is fabricated. Beat: triumph shadowed by fear he'll destroy it.

chapters.title: What Hume Offers
chapters.summary: Hume privately offers Quentin her old career back, fully restored, if she hands over the page and walks away from Marisol. Beat: temptation aimed exactly at her oldest wound.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Quentin records the offer and refuses. She chooses the woman and the town over the identity she mourned for five years. Beat: character climax — the vow made to herself.

chapters.title: Wedding Morning
chapters.summary: The wedding proceeds on the beach despite the condemnation order, the town physically standing between bailiffs and the altar. Beat: communal defiance rendered joyful.

chapters.title: Vows and Evidence
chapters.summary: During the ceremony, Quentin presents the deed page and Bram's testimony to the assembled crowd and a sympathetic county judge who attends as a guest. Beat: climax — justice performed in front of everyone.

chapters.title: The Order Falls
chapters.summary: The judge voids the eviction pending fraud investigation; Hume is escorted out mid-reception as tenants cheer. Priya's wedding continues around the wreckage of his ambitions. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: After the Guests Leave
chapters.summary: Quiet aftermath: Quentin and Marisol clean the bakery together, exhausted and new. Quentin admits she's scared to stay. Beat: tender uncertainty.

chapters.title: The Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: At the station, ticket in hand, Quentin watches the train go without boarding. She walks back to Larkspur Lane. Beat: the blurb's promise fulfilled — choosing to stay.

chapters.title: Second Chances, Better Timing
chapters.summary: Epilogue-ish: weeks later, Quentin reopens her planning business in Port Alder, specializing in small honest weddings. Marisol names a pastry after her. Beat: earned joy, found family complete.

chapters.title: The Vow of Port Alder
chapters.summary: Final chapter, alternating POVs. At the bakery's renewal signing, Quentin and Marisol exchange private vows witnessed by Edda, Theo, and Bram — not a wedding, something better: a promise kept in daylight. Beat: thematic resolution; love as staying.
